name: Restructure and defer lease payments
summary: Small business customers who hit a cash flow problem ask, through customer service or their collector, to skip payments for a few months or stretch the remaining term. A lease administration specialist gathers the customer's reasons and financial information, checks the request against the restructure policy and any securitisation limits, models a new schedule, gets a senior credit analyst's approval and a manager's sign-off, sends an amending agreement for the customer and guarantors to sign, and rebooks the contract so billing, collections and the funders see the change. The work takes two to four weeks, mostly waiting for customers, guarantors and approvers, and in 2020 the same process was swamped by waves of COVID deferral requests.

baseline.org_archetype: A mid-size Canadian independent equipment lessor with about 55,000 active contracts, about 65% of receivables sold to bank-sponsored conduits, a lease system that supports due date, term and payment changes, and e-signature for amendments.
baseline.notes: Describes case-by-case handling at the normal volume of about 90 requests a month. In spring 2020 lessors handled hundreds or thousands of deferral requests a month through simplified standard programs; that peak is described in the assumptions rather than modelled step by step.

trigger: Customer service routes a customer's request to defer or restructure, or an early- or late-stage collector refers a customer with a temporary cash flow problem.
end_state: The signed amendment is rebooked and billing, collections, treasury and the customer have the new schedule, or the request is declined or withdrawn and the account is back with collections.

volume.seasonality: Rises in downturns and in sectors with seasonal cash flow (agriculture, construction in winter); the 1,500 high end is the spring 2020 COVID wave.

evidence.note: Range from the organisation file's process map; the 2020 peak is supported by CFLA's surveys (a fifth of members saw requests from over half the portfolio) and ELFA's 7.4% of portfolio deferred in 2020. The mode of 90 is tier C.

About 3 hours of specialist time per request at 90 requests a month. The organisation file leaves about 3 FTE of this role unclaimed. At the 2020 peak of up to 1,500 requests the work could not be done this way; see assumptions. Cost from the organisation file.
Wage basis from Job Bank NOC 11109, loaded as in the organisation file. FTE is a tier C estimate: about 50 minutes per credit review on about 75 requests a month.
Wage basis from Job Bank NOC 10021. FTE is a tier C estimate for sign-off of terms.
Confirms arrears and holds collection on referrals from early-stage collections. FTE tier C.
Confirms arrears, notices and guarantor position on referrals from late-stage collections. FTE tier C.
Approves restructures above the analyst's authority, about 15% of reviews. Cost from the organisation file.
Approves exceptions to the restructure policy, about 5% of requests. Cost from the organisation file.
Checks conduit limits for securitised contracts whose maturity moves. Not listed for this process in the organisation file's process map, but the role exists there. Cost from the organisation file.

systems.name: Lease management system (contracts, schedules, billing, tax codes, asset records, servicing)
Document imaging and contract file store
Spreadsheet models (pool cuts, borrowing base, covenants, budget, tax workpapers)
Commercial and consumer credit bureau portals (Equifax, PayNet)
Provincial personal property registry and Quebec RDPRM search and registration portals
Customer relationship management system (partner accounts, pipeline, commissions data)

steps.name: Log the restructure request and open the case
steps.description: A lease administration specialist picks up the request from the team's work queue (a task from customer service or a referral note from collections), checks for an open request on the same customer, and notes the contract status, arrears, total exposure across the customer's contracts, whether the contract is in a securitisation pool and whether it is a Quebec contract needing French documents.

evidence.note: Referral sources follow the organisation file's process map; shares are estimates from the referral rates in the collections workflows.

steps.name: Early-stage collector confirms arrears and holds collection
steps.description: The collector who referred the account adds the current arrears, returned debits, promises made and broken and the customer's stated reason to the case, and sets a hold code so automated notices and calls stop while the request is decided.

error.defect_description: Hold not set, so the customer keeps getting collection calls during review.

evidence.note: Referral criteria and collection pause are described in efc-collect-early-stage s14 and s15; times are estimates.

steps.name: Late-stage collector confirms arrears, notices and guarantors
steps.description: The late-stage collector records the arrears, whether a default notice or section 244 notice has gone out and when its period ends, the guarantors' position and any insolvency search result, and holds enforcement while the request is decided.

evidence.note: Based on efc-collect-late-stage s11; times are estimates.

steps.name: Send the restructure application and ask for financial information
steps.description: The specialist e-mails the customer the restructure application: the reason for the difficulty, how long it is expected to last, what they propose (deferral of a number of payments, lower payments for a period, term extension), recent bank statements or interim financial statements, and for larger exposures the latest annual statements and a cash flow forecast.

evidence.note: Typical hardship application content; no source opened describes a Canadian lessor's form.

steps.name: Customer returns the application and financials
steps.description: The case waits for the customer to complete the form and gather statements. Small business owners in difficulty are slow to respond, and some find other money or government support and drop the request.

evidence.note: CFLA reported that government programs led over 60% of customers to withdraw deferral requests in April 2020. Waiting times and the 30% incomplete share are tier C.

steps.name: Chase missing information
steps.description: The specialist calls or e-mails the customer about missing statements or an unsigned application, and reminds them that collection activity resumes if the request is not completed. Customers who do not reply after the follow-up are returned to collections.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Check eligibility against the restructure policy
steps.description: The specialist checks the request against the restructure policy: payments made since booking, earlier deferrals on the contract, arrears not past the policy limit, no insolvency filing, equipment still in use and in the customer's hands, and for securitised contracts whether a deferral or new maturity is allowed under the conduit agreement.

control.basis: Restructure and deferral policy: eligibility criteria and limits on repeat deferrals

next.condition: outside policy but worth an exception

evidence.note: Servicing limits on modifications are described in the prospectus; standard deferral programs were common in 2020 per CFLA. The shares are tier C.

steps.name: Model the restructure options and new schedule
steps.description: The specialist builds the proposal in the lease system's quote screens and a spreadsheet: which payments are deferred and whether they are added to the end or spread over the remaining term, the new maturity date, any deferral fee and extra interest, sales tax on the new payment amounts, and whether the new maturity stays within the equipment's useful life and the registration period.

error.defect_description: Calculation error in the new schedule, fee or tax.

evidence.note: Due date change, lease extension, term change, payment change and extension fee transactions are documented. Times are tier C.

steps.name: Review the restructure for credit
steps.description: A senior credit analyst refreshes the commercial bureau report, reads the financial information and payment history, looks at the customer's total exposure and the equipment's value against the balance, and recommends approval, approval with conditions (a partial payment now, an added guarantor, a shorter deferral) or decline, within delegated authority. The analyst is independent of the collector who referred the account.

error.defect_description: A weak customer is approved and defaults later.

control.basis: Credit policy: delegated credit authority for modifications, with credit review separate from collections

evidence.note: The process map names a senior credit analyst as approver. Shares and times are tier C.

steps.name: Check conduit limits for a securitised contract
steps.description: For a contract sold to a conduit whose maturity or payment dates will move, a securitisation analyst checks the purchase and servicing agreement: deferrals allowed only for contracts in default, no new maturity past the pool's latest maturity, and limits on modified contracts. Where the change is not allowed the analyst arranges to repurchase the contract from the pool at the next settlement.

error.defect_description: A pool limit is missed and the modification breaches the servicing agreement.

control.basis: Conduit purchase and servicing agreement: servicer covenants on payment deferrals, maturity extensions and repurchase of modified contracts

evidence.note: Servicer covenants on modifications and possible acquisition of extended leases are described in the prospectus. Times are tier C.

steps.name: Approve the terms and any fee waiver
steps.description: The lease administration manager checks the calculation against the credit approval, confirms the documents to be used, approves any waiver of the deferral fee or arrears interest within their limit and signs off the offer. Calculations that do not tie go back to the specialist.

control.basis: Maker-checker approval of contract modifications and fee waivers by a manager other than the preparer

evidence.note: Common control; times are estimates.

steps.name: Approve an exception to the restructure policy
steps.description: The vice-president of operations reviews requests outside the policy, such as a third deferral, an extension beyond the usual limit or waived interest for a large customer, weighing the expected loss on repossession against the concession, and approves or declines.

control.basis: Restructure policy exception authority held by the vice-president of operations

evidence.note: The process map lists the vice-president of operations; the trigger for this approval is the author's assumption.

steps.name: Approve a restructure above the analyst's authority
steps.description: The director of collections and recoveries reviews large or high-risk restructures and late-stage accounts above the analyst's limit, compares the restructure with the recovery expected from repossession, and approves, adds conditions or declines.

control.basis: Delegated authority matrix for restructures by exposure and delinquency

evidence.note: The process map lists the director of collections; shares and times are estimates.

steps.name: Prepare the amendment and send it for signature
steps.description: The specialist fills the amending agreement template with the deferred payments, new schedule, maturity, fees and a confirmation that all other terms and the guarantees continue, adds a guarantor acknowledgement, produces it in French for Quebec customers, and sends it by e-signature with a cover note explaining the new debit dates and amounts.

error.defect_description: Amendment terms differ from the approval.

control.basis: Legal requirements for amendments: written amendment kept in the lease file, guarantor consent to preserve the guarantee, French-language documents for Quebec customers

evidence.note: Written amendments kept in the lease file are a securitisation representation in the prospectus. Guarantor consent and French documents are tier C practice.

steps.name: Customer and guarantors sign the amendment
steps.description: The case waits for the customer and each guarantor to sign. Guarantors who are not involved in the business are the usual delay.

next.condition: not signed by the offer expiry

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Check the signed amendment
steps.description: The specialist checks that every party signed and dated, that the guarantor acknowledgement is complete and that the signed version matches the approved terms, then files it to the contract in imaging. Missing signatures are sent back out.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Rebook the contract in the lease system
steps.description: The specialist enters the change in the lease system: due date change or payment deferral, term extension, new payment amounts and fee, so the system rebuilds the payment schedule, income and tax, clears the arrears that were capitalised, flags the contract as modified for risk and funder reporting, and updates the debit schedule.

error.defect_description: Schedule, fee or tax keyed differently from the amendment.

evidence.note: Servicing system transactions for due date, term and payment changes. Times are tier C.

steps.name: Peer check the rebooked schedule
steps.description: A second specialist compares the new schedule, maturity, fee, tax and modification flag in the lease system with the signed amendment and the approval, and returns errors for correction.

control.basis: Maker-checker review of contract changes in the lease system

next.condition: new maturity passes the registration expiry

evidence.note: Common control; shares and times are estimates.

steps.name: Renew or amend the security registration
steps.description: When the new maturity falls after the PPSA or RDPRM registration expires, the specialist files a financing change statement through the registry portal to extend the registration period and saves the verification statement to the file.

error.defect_description: Registration renewed for too short a period.

control.basis: Personal property security acts: a registration lapses at the end of its period unless renewed by a financing change statement before expiry (BC PPSA s.44(2) and equivalents)

evidence.note: Renewal by financing change statement before expiry. Share of cases is tier C.

steps.name: Notify billing, collections, treasury and risk
steps.description: The specialist sends the contract amendment to billing so the next invoices and debits follow the new schedule with the required pre-notification, closes the referral and releases the hold in the collections system, adds a securitised contract to the month's pool change notice for treasury, and confirms the new schedule to the customer.
outputs: contract amendment to billing and customer

error.defect_description: Billing not told in time, so a debit at the old amount goes out and returns.

control.basis: Payments Canada Rule H1 s.17: pre-notification of a changed PAD amount or date at least 10 calendar days before the debit, unless waived in the PAD agreement

evidence.note: Pre-notification rule from Rule H1. Hand-offs follow the organisation file's process map.

steps.name: Send the decline and return the account to collections
steps.description: The specialist writes to the customer that the request is declined with the reason in plain terms, notes the decision, removes the collection hold and returns the account to the referring collector with the date collection activity resumes.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Close a withdrawn or unsigned request
steps.description: When the customer withdraws, stops replying or lets the signed offer expire, the specialist closes the case with the reason, voids any open e-signature envelope, removes the hold and tells the referring collector so collection activity resumes.

evidence.note: Withdrawals were common once government support arrived in 2020. Times are tier C.

exceptions.name: Incomplete application
exceptions.description: Statements or the signed form are missing; the specialist chases, and about four in ten of these customers withdraw or stop replying.

exceptions.name: Securitised contract whose maturity moves
exceptions.description: Treasury checks the conduit agreement and may repurchase the contract from the pool before it is modified.

exceptions.name: Approval above authority or policy exception
exceptions.description: Large or late-stage restructures go to the director of collections; requests outside policy go to the vice-president of operations.

exceptions.name: Declined
exceptions.description: Ineligible under the policy or declined on credit; the account returns to collections.

exceptions.name: Rebooking error
exceptions.description: The peer check finds the new schedule, fee or tax keyed wrongly and sends it back.

exceptions.name: Registration renewal
exceptions.description: The new maturity passes the registration expiry, so a financing change statement is filed.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from the request reaching lease administration to rebooked, declined or withdrawn
benchmarks.population: Author's estimate for case-by-case restructures at a mid-size lessor

evidence.note: No published cycle time was found. Built from the customer's time to send financial information, the credit review queue, signature by guarantors and the rebooking queue.

benchmarks.unit: share of portfolio (US equipment finance, by value)
benchmarks.population: ELFA Survey of Equipment Finance Activity respondents, 2020

benchmarks.unit: share of customers withdrawing requests after government programs were announced (more than)
share of CFLA respondents accommodating at least 80% of deferral requests (more than)
calendar days before a changed debit amount or date
benchmarks.population: PADs at set intervals in Canada, unless waived

pain_points.description: Most of the elapsed time is waiting for the customer's financial information and for guarantors to sign, while the account sits on collection hold and arrears grow.

evidence.note: Estimate.

pain_points.description: Securitised contracts need a check of conduit limits and sometimes a repurchase before they can be modified, adding a hand-off to treasury.
The new schedule is modelled in a spreadsheet and keyed again into the lease system, so calculation and keying errors need a manager's check and a peer check.

evidence.note: Estimate.

pain_points.description: A case-by-case process with several approvals cannot absorb a wave of requests; in 2020 lessors faced deferral requests from up to half their portfolios and more than 100 COVID calls a day.
If billing is not told in time, a debit at the old amount goes out after the amendment, returns and restarts collection activity.

evidence.note: Estimate.

Read from a text copy saved under scratch/ by earlier work.

assumptions: The model describes normal-volume case-by-case handling (mode 90 a month). In spring 2020, with up to 1,500 requests a month, lessors used a standard deferral program (for example three months deferred and added to the end) with a short application, no financial statements and manager sign-off; that path is the s07 to s11 branch, which carries only 10% of cases at the mode. At 1,500 a month even the short path would need many more people than lease administration has, so customer service, collections and credit staff were redeployed.

About 53% of requests end restructured, 20% declined and 27% withdrawn or unsigned; these shares are estimates for normal times, when lessors are stricter than the 80%-plus acceptance many reported in 2020. Referral shares (40% customer service, 35% early-stage, 25% late-stage collections) are estimates consistent with the referral rates in the existing collections workflows.
The securitisation analyst is added for the conduit check although the process map does not list that role for this process; the organisation file has it.

The vice-president of operations approves policy exceptions and the director of collections approves restructures above the senior analyst's authority; the split of authority is the author's assumption.
Accounting for the modification (IFRS 16 lessor modification and IFRS 9 modification gain or loss) is done by the lease system and the month-end close, not as a step here.

About 3 hours of specialist time per request is the author's estimate; at 90 requests a month that is about 2 FTE of the 3 FTE of lease administration specialists left unclaimed in the organisation file.
Loaded hourly costs are the organisation file's (wage times 1.35).
